# The stationary Adam field {#sec-adam-field}

## Nonlinear fading memory

In @sec-momentum, linear memory preserved the entire frozen field:
$\Eunder{\statlawtheta}{\Mtheta}=\htheta$. Adam adds a second-moment
memory and divides the momentum by the regularised square root of that
memory. Fix $0\leq\alpha,\beta<1$ and $\eps>0$,
and consider the controlled observations of @eq-controlled-transition with

$$
\Momentumupdate,
$$ {#eq-adam-m}

$$
\Secondmomentupdate,
$$ {#eq-adam-v}

$$
\Adamupdate.
$$ {#eq-adam-update}

Squares, square roots, division, and the product $\odot$ are componentwise;
the scalar $\eps$ is added in each coordinate. Initially take
$M_0\in\R^d$ and $V_0\in[0,\infty)^d$, measurable with respect to
$\cF_0$. These are uncorrected memories, with no finite-time bias factors.
We view this as an SA mechanism, without requiring $H$ to be a gradient.
The two memories are linear filters of the signal and its square, but
their data-dependent normalisation is nonlinear: this is where the
mean-field preservation argument of @prp-momentum-field ceases to apply.

## Frozen memories and the candidate drift

Fix $\theta$ and work under the stationary path law $\statlawtheta$ of
@sec-controlled-markov-sa. Throughout the frozen construction assume
$\pitheta(\norm{\Htheta}^2)<\infty$. Alongside $\Mtheta$ from
@eq-frozen-momentum, define

$$
\Vtheta:=(1-\beta)\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}
  \beta^j\Htheta(X_{-j}^\theta)^{\odot2}.
$$ {#eq-frozen-second-moment}

When a memory coefficient is zero, its series means just its $j=0$ term.
For each coordinate $i$, Tonelli's theorem and stationarity give

$$
\Eunder{\statlawtheta}{V_i^\theta}
=(1-\beta)\sum_{j\geq0}\beta^j
  \pitheta(H_{\theta,i}^2)
=\pitheta(H_{\theta,i}^2)<\infty.
$$

Thus the nonnegative series is finite almost surely and integrable;
its partial sums converge in $L^1$ as well, since their expected tails
are $\beta^{J+1}\pitheta(H_{\theta,i}^2)$ after index $J$.
The same moment assumption implies the hypothesis of
@lem-stationary-momentum-exists, so $\Mtheta$ exists in $L^1$.
Neither argument uses independence.

::: {#def-stationary-adam-field}
## Stationary Adam field

Under these frozen moment assumptions, put
$W^\theta:=(\sqrt{\Vtheta}+\eps)^{-1}$ and
$A^\theta:=\Mtheta\odot W^\theta$. The *stationary Adam field* is

$$
\Ftheta:=\Eunder{\statlawtheta}{A^\theta}
=\Eunder{\statlawtheta}{\Adamratio{\Mtheta}{\Vtheta}}.
$$ {#eq-stationary-adam-field}

:::

This expectation exists because $0<W_i^\theta\leq\eps^{-1}$ and
$\norm{A^\theta}\leq\eps^{-1}\norm{\Mtheta}$. Unlike
$\htheta=\meanfieldtheta$, which uses only a one-time marginal,
$\Ftheta$ uses the stationary path law through both fading histories.
It is a candidate frozen drift, not yet an ODE approximation for the
actual adaptive recursion @eq-adam-update. Regularity in $\theta$ is
not a consequence of this pointwise definition.

## Relation to the IID Adam field

@Dereich2025_UJMNX8NK [Definition 1.3] define the corresponding field
by averaging the normalised momentum computed from an infinite IID history.
Their Lemma 3.1 gives a bounded, $1$-Lipschitz history map in a specific
weighted sequence norm; with their locally $p$-regular innovation
(Definition 1.4), the field is bounded and locally Lipschitz when
$\alpha<\sqrt\beta$. That lemma recalls earlier work by Dereich and
Jentzen, rather than proving a new history-map estimate.[^adam-history-source]

For IID innovations, their Theorem 1.5 gives localised finite-horizon
ODE tracking under local $p$-regularity, $p\geq2$, and positive,
non-summable, decreasing gains tending to zero with their step-size
regularity condition (10). With
$\sum_n\gamma_n^{1+p/3}<\infty$, Corollary 1.9 gives the APT property
on the event of bounded iterates. Corollary 1.10 requires any limit
in probability to be a zero of the Adam field. As discussed after
Definition 1.4, that field can have different zeros and directions
from the ordinary mean field [@Dereich2025_UJMNX8NK].
Their Definition 1.1 uses a finite-time second-moment bias correction;
the stationary history functional agrees with ours, but the finite
recursion differs. Neither their IID theorem nor that agreement proves
the controlled-Markov APT result sought here.

[^adam-history-source]: @DereichJentzen2024, Lemma 3.1 and equation (148).
    The former proves the deterministic history-map bound and Lipschitz
    estimate; the latter bounds the induced field's parameter variation.
    These are the results explicitly recalled in Lemma 3.1 of
    @Dereich2025_UJMNX8NK.

## A pathwise bound on the normalised momentum

The boundedness part of the cited history-map estimate has a short
proof that does not involve a probability law.

::: {#lem-adam-readout-bounded}
## Uniform bound for normalised histories

Suppose $0\leq\alpha<\sqrt\beta<1$. For a scalar history
$(z_j)_{j\geq0}$ with $\sum_j\beta^jz_j^2<\infty$, set

$$
m=(1-\alpha)\sum_{j\geq0}\alpha^jz_j,
\qquad v=(1-\beta)\sum_{j\geq0}\beta^jz_j^2.
$$

Then the numerator converges absolutely and

$$
\frac{\abs{m}}{\sqrt v+\eps}
\leq c_{\alpha,\beta}
:=\frac{1-\alpha}
  {\sqrt{1-\beta}\sqrt{1-\alpha^2/\beta}}.
$$ {#eq-adam-scalar-bound}

Applying this coordinatewise to vector histories gives the Euclidean
bound $\norm{A}\leq C_{\alpha,\beta,d}:=\sqrt d\,c_{\alpha,\beta}$.
:::

::: {.proof}
Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz, first for partial sums and then for the
nonnegative series of absolute values, gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
(1-\alpha)\sum_{j\geq0}\alpha^j\abs{z_j}
&\leq(1-\alpha)
  \left[\sum_{j\geq0}(\alpha^2/\beta)^j\right]^{1/2}
  \left[\sum_{j\geq0}\beta^jz_j^2\right]^{1/2}\\
&=c_{\alpha,\beta}\sqrt v.
\end{aligned}
$$

Division by $\sqrt v+\eps$ proves @eq-adam-scalar-bound, including
$v=0$. Summing squared coordinate bounds proves the vector assertion.
:::

This estimate is deterministic and pathwise; it applies to stationary
Markov histories just as to IID histories. It bounds $\Ftheta$ uniformly
wherever the frozen moment assumption holds, but supplies no parameter
regularity or controlled-Markov ODE theorem.

## Bounded velocity and adaptive-MCMC validity

For the actual recursion, now take $M_0=V_0=0$ and
$\alpha<\sqrt\beta$. Unrolling both memories gives a finite history
of the actual signals $H_{\theta_{k-1}}(X_k)$, padded with zeros.
@lem-adam-readout-bounded therefore yields, without freezing parameters,

$$
\norm{\theta_{n+1}-\theta_n}
\leq C_{\alpha,\beta,d}\gamma_{n+1}.
$$ {#eq-adam-bounded-velocity}

This uniform constant does not cover arbitrary initial memories without
an additional compatibility bound. Bounded velocity is not parameter
convergence.

Suppose also that $\gamma_n\to0$, $\pitheta\equiv\pi$, the parameters
remain in the admissible set, and the frozen family satisfies

$$
\sup_x d_{\mathrm{TV}}\bigl(\Ptheta(x,\cdot),\Pvartheta(x,\cdot)\bigr)
\leq L\norm{\theta-\vartheta},
\qquad\theta,\vartheta\in\ThetaSet.
$$ {#eq-adam-kernel-lipschitz}

Here $d_{\mathrm{TV}}(\mu,\nu):=\sup_B\abs{\mu(B)-\nu(B)}$.
This is assumption (A8) of @Laitinen2024_G3FDZQA8. In particular,

$$
D_n:=\sup_x d_{\mathrm{TV}}\bigl(
 P_{\theta_n}(x,\cdot),P_{\theta_{n-1}}(x,\cdot)\bigr)
\leq LC_{\alpha,\beta,d}\gamma_n\longrightarrow0.
$$ {#eq-adam-diminishing-adaptation}

For measurability one may use the deterministic upper bound
$\min\{1,LC_{\alpha,\beta,d}\gamma_n\}$ in place of the supremum.
This gives their diminishing adaptation (A6), in fact pathwise.
Their Lemma 10 implies weak $1$-waning; here Cesàro averaging also
directly gives $n^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^nD_k\to0$ almost surely, their
*strong $1$-waning* condition (A5). Lemma 16 treats the general
SA-sized-increment mechanism [@Laitinen2024_G3FDZQA8].

An LLN needs more. Under their adapted controlled-transition setup
(A1), the common target, and simultaneous uniform ergodicity (A3),

$$
\sup_{\theta\in\ThetaSet}\sup_x
 d_{\mathrm{TV}}\bigl(P_\theta^k(x,\cdot),\pi\bigr)
\leq C\rho^k,
\qquad k\geq0,\quad C<\infty,\quad0\leq\rho<1,
$$

Theorem 9(ii) then gives
$n^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^nf(X_k)\to\pi(f)$ almost surely for every fixed
bounded measurable $f$ [@Laitinen2024_G3FDZQA8]. Neither common
invariance nor diminishing adaptation alone establishes this conclusion.
Keeping $\theta_n$ in the admissible set is essential; their Remark 15
discusses stabilisation, which requires specifying the actual algorithm.
This sampling-validity conclusion does not require parameter convergence
and does not identify its equilibria: it can coexist with nonconvergent
adaptation or an Adam equilibrium different from a Robbins--Monro root.

## Covariance and Robbins--Monro roots

Return to the frozen moment assumptions of
@def-stationary-adam-field; the following identities require no
restriction $\alpha<\sqrt\beta$. All expectations and covariances in
this subsection are under $\statlawtheta$. Since $\Mtheta$ is
integrable and $W^\theta$ is bounded, all coordinate products below
are integrable. By @prp-momentum-field,

$$
F_i(\theta)
=h_i(\theta)\E[W_i^\theta]
 +\Cov(M_i^\theta,W_i^\theta).
$$

Define the *componentwise covariance vector*, not a covariance matrix,
by $\Cov_{\odot}(M,W)_i:=\Cov(M_i,W_i)$. Thus

$$
\Ftheta
=\htheta\odot\E[W^\theta]
 +\Cov_{\odot}(\Mtheta,W^\theta).
$$ {#eq-adam-covariance-decomposition}

This is exact: expand each covariance as
$\E[M_i^\theta W_i^\theta]-\E[M_i^\theta]\E[W_i^\theta]$
and use $\E[M_i^\theta]=h_i(\theta)$.

::: {#prp-adam-root-covariance}
## A covariance criterion at a Robbins--Monro root

Let $\theta^\star$ satisfy the frozen moment assumptions and
$h(\theta^\star)=0$. Then

$$
F(\theta^\star)
=\Cov_{\odot}(M^{\theta^\star},W^{\theta^\star}).
$$ {#eq-adam-field-at-rm-root}

Consequently $\theta^\star$ is also an Adam root if and only if
$\Cov(M_i^{\theta^\star},W_i^{\theta^\star})=0$ for every coordinate.
:::

::: {.proof}
Substitute $h(\theta^\star)=0$ in
@eq-adam-covariance-decomposition. The vector vanishes exactly when
all its coordinates vanish.
:::

A zero stationary numerator mean is therefore insufficient: the random
normalisation uses the same history, and root correspondence requires
additional structure in the joint law. Conversely, an Adam root with
$\htheta\ne0$ would satisfy the cancellation identity
$\htheta\odot\E[W^\theta]=-\Cov_{\odot}(\Mtheta,W^\theta)$.
There is no general reason for the two root sets to agree in either
direction; this is not a claim that they differ in every model.

Both memories use $(\ldots,X_{-1}^\theta,X_0^\theta)$.
Even IID observations can create numerator--normaliser dependence
through shared inputs; Markov observations introduce additional lagged
dependence. Two frozen kernels with the same invariant marginal can
therefore, in principle, give different Adam fields through their
different stationary path laws. No such counterexample is asserted here.

The memory existence, field integrability, pathwise bound, and covariance
criterion above are direct derivations. Controlled-Markov Adam APT
convergence, parameter regularity of $F$, existence or uniqueness of
equilibria, parameter convergence, and any augmented-state transfer of
mixing or Poisson estimates remain unproved. @sec-iid-to-markov takes
up the passage from IID histories to controlled Markov histories.
